major_work.title: 중국 AI 컴퓨팅 소프트웨어 자립과 HBM 수요를 분리해서 봐야 한다

CONFIRMED: Reuters 2026-09-30 reported DeepSeek and Huawei are collaborating on open-source programming infrastructure for Huawei Ascend AI chips, including compute/communication libraries and TileLang, with the stated goal of reducing reliance on Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem.
KMB issue-digest generated 2026-10-01 01:11 KST is HEALTHY with 20 sources checked, 223 raw items and 213 deduplicated items.
The current KMB issues dataset did not contain a DeepSeek/Huawei issue at this run's preflight, so this fresh discovery is not yet represented by a related_issue_id.
HYPOTHESIS: China reducing CUDA/software dependence can weaken Nvidia ecosystem lock-in without proportionally reducing advanced-memory demand. If Ascend deployment scales, accelerator substitution may change GPU vendor share while aggregate HBM/advanced-memory bit demand remains supported by AI compute growth.

For Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the key transmission variable may be China accelerator unit growth × HBM capacity per accelerator × domestic Chinese HBM substitution rate, rather than Nvidia China share alone.
UNKNOWN: Actual Ascend 950 shipment volumes and ramp timing
HBM capacity/type per Ascend configuration and supplier mix
Chinese domestic HBM yield, qualification and volume ramp
Export-control/licensing constraints affecting Korean memory shipments into China
Whether software portability materially changes training/inference TCO and adoption

major_work.why_important: A headline such as 'China reduces Nvidia dependence' can be misread as automatically bearish for Korean memory. Compute-vendor substitution and memory-content substitution are separate causal links and should be tested independently.
impact_path: DeepSeek/Huawei software tooling improves Ascend usability
Ascend adoption can rise relative to Nvidia in China
Total AI compute and memory bits may still grow
Korean HBM demand depends on memory content/supplier substitution, not GPU share alone
major_work.counter_scenario: If Chinese HBM suppliers scale qualification/yield rapidly, export controls tighten, or Ascend designs materially reduce imported HBM content, Nvidia share loss could coincide with lower Samsung/SK Hynix China AI-memory demand.

handoff.AI_C: Build a scenario table/event study using Ascend shipment proxies × HBM content assumptions × Chinese HBM substitution rates; do not output probability until authoritative shipment/memory-content samples exist.
handoff.AI_B: Falsify the decoupling thesis: test whether Ascend adoption is actually paired with domestic-memory substitution, export-control tightening, lower HBM content, or weaker economics versus Nvidia.
